native_result.query: Between 3400 BCE to 3000 BCE, how does the number of monuments and axes changes with elements of symbolic capital?
native_result.HypoA: Between 3400 BCE to 3000 BCE, the number of monuments and axes increases along with symbolic capital
native_result.HypoB: HYPOTHESIS (3400-3000 BCE). Monument Count and Axes & Celts show distinct, asymmetric associations with the three symbolic-capital elements across this 400-year window. Monument Count is (i) weakly positively correlated with HatchetSword (Pearson r ≈ +0.21 to +0.28, Spearman ρ ≈ +0.26 to +0.33, p < 1e-4 across the linearly-interpolated, forward-fill and centennial layers) and (ii) moderately-to-strongly negatively correlated with HouseSize (r ≈ -0.40 in the linear-interpolation layer and r ≈ -0.61 in the forward-fill layer, ρ ≈ -0.39 to -0.63, p < 1e-16 in all three layers), so larger houses in 3400-3000 BCE co-occur with fewer, not more, monuments; (iii) Monument Count shows no measurable co-variation with Dagger because the Dagger Z-score is essentially constant at -0.58 throughout the window (sd = 0) in both time_series_data and capital.csv, so the dagger stock cannot have moved with monument-building in this 400-year slice. Axes & Celts behaves as a much weaker echo of the same pattern: (iv) weakly positive rank-correlation with HatchetSword (Spearman ρ ≈ +0.26 to +0.27 across all three layers is sign-consistent, whereas Pearson r flips between +0.03 in the linear-interpolation layer and -0.14 in the forward-fill layer, so Spearman is the tie-break and a positive rank-order co-variation is the most defensible reading, with ρ ≤ 0.27 as the main caveat); (v) again no association with Dagger (zero predictor variance); and (vi) weakly negative correlation with HouseSize (r ≈ -0.22 to -0.26, ρ ≈ -0.32 to -0.37, p < 1e-6 across all layers). The archaeological reading is that 3400-3000 BCE was a period in which monument accumulation intensified in step with rising HatchetSword signal but in counter-cycle with HouseSize, while axes & celts circulated too weakly and too coarsely-grained (only one sizeable spike at 3200 BCE, ZBeil = +2.60) to register a strong signal on any of the three symbolic-capital axes.
native_result.WorkflowB: Executed a single analysis.py that (1) loads all three CSVs with decimal=',' to handle European comma-decimals in capital.csv and the pollen file; (2) aligns axes by mapping capital.csv BCE -> CE_signed with CE = -BCE so all datasets share the time_series CE convention; (3) slices to the window CE ∈ [-3400, -3000] (yielding 401 rows in time_series and the pollen file, 5 rows in capital.csv); (4) constructs a Layer B forward-fill staircase on the time_series _inter series so each 100-year bin carries the value at its century anchor, breaking the linearity assumption; (5) computes six predictor × outcome cells against two outcomes (MonumentCount, AxesCelts) and three predictors (HatchetSword, Dagger, HouseSize), each on three data layers (A: time_series _inter, B: forward-fill, C: capital.csv centennial), producing Pearson r, Spearman ρ, OLS slope with 95% confidence interval, and their p-values; (6) dispatches synthesis: sign from Pearson/OLS with Spearman tiebreak, magnitude bins |r|<0.1 negligible, 0.1-0.3 weak, 0.3-0.5 moderate, ≥0.5 strong; (7) writes artifacts/analysis/regression_grid.csv and artifacts/analysis/synthesis.json; (8) prints a formatted summary table to artifacts/analysis/run_output.txt for downstream verification.
